raw_response:
I am 73 years old, and my legs aren't what they used to be after fifty years in these fields. But I know every corner of my 2.6 mu plot, and I know cotton is what this land does best. My wife and I manage this together — our children have gone to the city — so I cannot take on anything too labor-heavy. I also will not waste money on fancy inputs I do not need.

This year, I will plant cotton on the full 2.6 mu. I will buy the improved cotton seeds from the county supply store — not the most expensive hybrid, but the kind my neighbors and I have used for years that performs reliably in Quzhou's soil. In late April, I will use rotary tillage to prepare the seedbed, the same way I have always done.

For fertilizer, I will apply compound fertilizer as a base dressing before planting, and then topdress with urea when the plants flower. I do not believe in piling on chemicals — 15 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 10 kg of potassium per mu is enough for this soil. I have a well, so I can irrigate when the rains fail, but pumping water is hard work at my age, so I will irrigate only three times: once right after sowing to ensure good emergence, once at the flowering stage, and once when the bolls are filling. For pests, the bollworm and aphids always come, so I will spray four times through the season — only when I see them, not blindly.

I expect around 250 kg of seed cotton per mu. That has been my average, and at my age, steady is better than greedy.
